svg.title: What an unconditional floor does to the division of surplus
svg.desc: Left panel, additive case: the floor of value Delta raises the human party's disagreement payoff and the joint value of agreement by the same amount, so the frontier shifts out by Delta and the human party's payoff rises by exactly Delta while the surplus and its division are unchanged. Right panel, substitution case: the floor replaces floor goods the provider used to supply at cost c_s, so the frontier shifts out only by c_s; the surplus shrinks by Delta minus c_s, the human party gains between Delta over two and Delta, and the provider's payoff falls by at most Delta over two.
svg.text: human party better off by exactly Δ.
Surplus shrinks by Δ − c; human gain
between Δ/2 and Δ; provider loses at
Plotted with V = 10, d = (2, 2), Δ = 3, c = 1 and a symmetric Nash split. The working draft's claim
of a Δ/2 gain in every bargain was the substitution case misread as general.
